Read GeoSuite tables

Source: R/geo_suite.R
get_statcan_geo_suite.Rd

Reads a table of the Statistics Canada GeoSuite for the given census year. The GeoSuite has a table for each geographic level, with the codes and names of the areas, how they relate to other levels, population and dwelling counts, land areas and representative points, along with code tables like the census subdivision types. Called without level this lists the tables available for the census year.

The data comes from parquet files hosted at https://data.mountainmath.ca/census/geo_suite/, as Statistics Canada now blocks programmatic downloads of the GeoSuite. The files are derived from Statistics Canada data under the Statistics Canada Open Licence. They get downloaded on first use and cached if the cancensus cache path has been set, and cached copies only get updated with refresh = TRUE. Reading the tables requires the duckdb and DBI packages.

Usage

get_statcan_geo_suite(
  level = NULL,
  census_year = "2021",
  refresh = FALSE,
  language = getOption("cancensus.language", "en"),
  quiet = FALSE
)

Arguments

level

the table to read, e.g. "DA", "CSD" or "CMA_CA". "CMA", "CA" and "CMACA" read "CMA_CA", "LOC" reads "PN" and "CB" reads "DB". If NULL this returns the list of tables for the census year.

census_year

census year to get the data for, one of 1996, 2001, 2006, 2011, 2016 or 2021. For older censuses get_statcan_geographic_attributes() has much of the same information.

refresh

(logical) download the table again if true, and report if it has changed

language

language of the column labels and table titles, one of "en" or "fr". Defaults to the cancensus.language option, and to "en" if that is not set. This does not change the data.

quiet

(logical) suppress messages and the progress bar if TRUE. Warnings about failed downloads are still shown.

Value

tibble with the GeoSuite table, with a description of each column in its "label" attribute. The "metadata" attribute of the tibble holds the metadata of the table, including the attribution, licence, source and notes. If level is NULL, a tibble with the table names, their title and primary_key and the size of the file in bytes. If the data can't be downloaded this gives a warning, and returns the cached data when refreshing existing cached data and NULL otherwise.

Tables and columns

The GeoSuite is available for the censuses from 1996 to 2021. The tables differ between census years, for example 1996 has enumeration areas (EA) instead of dissemination areas and blocks, 2001 to 2006 have urban areas (UA) and 2011 on population centres (POPCTR). Tables ending in _P hold the parts of areas that span provinces or other areas. PN is the place name table, called LOC in the source.

Column names follow the attribute files from get_statcan_geographic_attributes(): the level, the measure and the census year, e.g. CSDUID, CSDPOP2021 or DARPLAT. The same columns have the same names across census years, and the tables can be joined to the attribute files without renaming. A suffix A marks counts of the previous census adjusted to the current boundaries, and C or AC corrected counts from the count review. Columns referring to other levels hold the code within the parent level as in the source, e.g. CSDCODE instead of CSDUID. Each column has a description in its "label" attribute, and the Statistics Canada field name in the source_field entry of the columns metadata.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# list the tables of the 2021 GeoSuite
get_statcan_geo_suite(census_year = "2021")
# read the dissemination areas
get_statcan_geo_suite("DA", "2021")
} # }
